title: Unit map into the tensor-diagonal base change
statement: Let $k$ be a commutative ring, $L$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $B,C$ commutative $L$-algebras, regarded as $k$-algebras by restriction. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(x\otimes y)(x\prime\otimes y\prime)=xx\prime\otimes yy\prime$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Put $R=L\otimes_kL$ and $D=B\otimes_kC$. Give $D$ its $R$-algebra structure through $\psi:R\to D$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda\prime\mapsto(\lambda1_B)\otimes(\lambda\prime1_C)$, and give $L$ its $R$-algebra structure through $\mu:R\to L$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda\prime\mapsto\lambda\lambda\prime$. There is a unique unital ring homomorphism $\alpha:B\otimes_LC\to D\otimes_RL$ such that $\alpha(b\otimes c)=(b\otimes c)\otimes1$ for all $b\in B,c\in C$. No injectivity, flatness, reducedness, finite-generation or field assumption is imposed; zero algebras are allowed.

proof.text: Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] supplies the commutative tensor rings $R,D$ and their unital inclusions. Clause (2) over $k$ constructs $\psi$ from the two $k$-algebra maps $\lambda\mapsto(\lambda1_B)\otimes1_C$ and $\lambda\mapsto1_B\otimes(\lambda1_C)$ into $D$, and constructs $\mu$ from the two identity maps of $L$. The two inputs for $\psi$ are composites of the given $k$-algebra maps $L\to B,C$ with the $k$-algebra inclusions from clause (1); hence they preserve the same $k$-structure, as clause (2) requires. Its pure-tensor formula gives exactly the $\psi,\mu$ specified in the statement. Hence the stated $R$-algebra structures are defined. Put $Q=D\otimes_RL$. Clause (1) gives unital ring maps $j:D\to Q$, $d\mapsto d\otimes1$, $i_B:B\to D$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and $i_C:C\to D$, $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. Give $Q$ its $L$-algebra structure through the right inclusion $\ell:L\to Q$, $\lambda\mapsto1_D\otimes\lambda$. Set $f=j\circ i_B$ and $g=j\circ i_C$.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, second proof paragraph displayed identity; explicit forward-map argument supplied by Q118 using Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: The bilinearity relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] in $Q$ give $(\psi(r)d)\otimes a=d\otimes\mu(r)a$ for $r\in R$, $d\in D$, $a\in L$, since both sides equal $r(d\otimes a)$. For $\lambda\in L$, specialize to $d=1_D$, $a=1$, and respectively $r=\lambda\otimes1$ and $r=1\otimes\lambda$. Since $\psi(\lambda\otimes1)=(\lambda1_B)\otimes1_C$, $\psi(1\otimes\lambda)=1_B\otimes(\lambda1_C)$, and both elements have $\mu$-image $\lambda$, this gives $f(\lambda1_B)=((\lambda1_B)\otimes1_C)\otimes1=1_D\otimes\lambda=(1_B\otimes(\lambda1_C))\otimes1=g(\lambda1_C)$. Hence both $f$ and $g$ respect the given $L$-structure maps, so they are $L$-algebra homomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, second proof paragraph displayed identity; explicit forward-map argument supplied by Q118 using Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] over $L$ to $f:B\to Q$ and $g:C\to Q$. It gives an $L$-algebra homomorphism $\alpha:B\otimes_LC\to Q$ with $\alpha(b\otimes c)=f(b)g(c)$. The tensor multiplications specified in the statement give $f(b)g(c)=((b\otimes1_C)\otimes1)((1_B\otimes c)\otimes1)=(b\otimes c)\otimes1$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, second proof paragraph displayed identity; explicit forward-map argument supplied by Q118 using Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Let $\alpha\prime$ be any unital ring map with the required pure-tensor formula. Taking $b=\lambda1_B$ and $c=1_C$ and using step 2 shows $\alpha\prime((\lambda1_B)\otimes1_C)=1_D\otimes\lambda=\ell(\lambda)$; thus $\alpha\prime$ is also an $L$-algebra homomorphism. Taking $c=1_C$ or $b=1_B$ shows its composites with the two tensor inclusions are $f$ and $g$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $\alpha\prime=\alpha$. Every construction used arbitrary commutative rings and unital maps, including zero rings.
